doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bud Powell living in Benny Harris's house
summary: Heath tells how Oscar Goodstein asked him to get Bud Powell home from Birdland, and how June was nervous with Bud in the house.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, I don’t know. Bud, he would look at you, and he would give you that grimace. You wouldn’t know if he was smiling or what. Bud was very strange at that time. Anyhow, he lived there, and at the time I was working in Birdland with him, Oscar Goodstein said, “Percy, see that Bud gets home,” ‘cause we’re living in the same house. We get in a cab to go from Birdland to the Bronx, and Bud would tell the cab driver, “Hey man, go through 115th Street. Percy, I’ll be right back.” He’d get out [of] the cab, I don’t know what building he went in, I’d sit there for a while, and I’d just tell the cab driver to take me home. And I told Oscar Goodstein, I cannot keep up with Bud Powell for you, so don’t assign me to be his keeper. It’s impossible. We lived in the same place, but you can’t get Bud Powell to go home when he wants to go out and do whatever he’s looking for.
